6. [CE1994/P2/Q52]
Suppose a country has an absolute advantage in good X. Which of the following is correct?

options.A: It is possible that the country has a higher opportunity cost of producing good X than another country.
options.B: The country can produce a greater amount of good X than another good with the same amount of resources.
options.C: The country will also have a comparative advantage in good X.
options.D: The country will have an absolute disadvantage in another good.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
7. [CE1996/P2/Q47]
A country will gain from international trade if

options.A: it specializes in producing goods in which it enjoys comparative advantage.
options.B: The price of its exports is higher than that of its imports.
options.C: The quantity of its exports is greater than the quantity of its imports.
options.D: The price of its imports is less than the unit cost of producing these goods itself.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
8. [CE1996/P2/Q53]
Which of the following economic principles can best explain why a doctor, who is the fastest typist in town, chooses to employ a typist to do all the typing for him?

options.D: law of diminishing returns

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
9. [CE1997/P2/Q48]
The production of good X involves two different tasks. When Mary focuses on one task and Peter on another, their total daily output is greater than that when each of them has to do both tasks. This can be explained by
(1) economies of scale.
(2) the principle of comparative advantage.
(3) the advantages of division of labour.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
10. [CE1998/P2/Q45]
If Country X can produce the same amount of each good with less resources than Country Y, then

options.A: there is no favourable terms of trade between Country X and Country Y.
options.B: Country Y may still produce some goods at a lower opportunity cost.
options.C: trade can still take place based on absolute advantage.
options.D: Country X possesses comparative advantage on all goods.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
11. [CE1999/P2/Q46]
If a country specializes and exports good X, it implies that

options.A: this country needs to give up less of other goods than other countries in order to produce good X.
options.B: this country has more resources than other countries for producing good X.
options.C: this country uses less resources than other countries for producing the same amount of good X.
options.D: this country can produce good X at a lower cost than other goods.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
12. [CE2000/P2/Q46]
Suppose there are good X and good Y only. If a country has a comparative advantage in good X, it will have

options.C: a comparative advantage in Y too.
options.D: a higher opportunity cost in producing Y.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
13. [CE2002/P2/Q44]
Suppose Mrs Wong, a sole proprietor of a garment factory, is the best cook in town, but she leaves all the cooking to her domestic helper at home. Which of the following would be correct?

options.A: The domestic helper has a comparative advantage in cooking.
options.B: Both Mrs Wong and the domestic helper provide a labour service and receive wages.
options.C: Complex division of labour is illustrated in this case.
options.D: Both Mrs Wong and the domestic helper are tertiary producers.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
14. [CE2002/P2/Q47]
Consider the trade between two countries X and Y, both of which produce garments and computers only. If country X has the comparative advantage in producing garments, then country X

options.A: produces more garments per unit of resources than country Y.
options.B: produces better quality garments than country Y.
options.C: gives up a smaller amount of computers in order to produce a unit of garments than country Y.
options.D: gains more from their trade than country Y.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
15. [CE2004/P2/Q45]
Both countries A and B produce goods X and Y. Under which of the following conditions does country A have a comparative advantage in the production of X?

options.A: One unit of X can be exchanged for more units of Y in country A than in country B.
options.B: In producing one unit of X, country A forgoes a smaller amount of Y than country B.
options.C: The opportunity cost of producing X in country A is smaller than that of Y in country B.
options.D: The amount of resources used in producing one unit of X is less in country A than in country B.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
16. [CE2006/P2/Q43]
Under free trade, a country exports computers and imports cars. Which of the following statements about the country must be correct?
The country

options.A: has an absolute advantage in producing cars.
options.B: has an absolute advantage in producing computers.
options.C: has a comparative disadvantage in producing cars.
options.D: requires less resources to produce each unit of computers.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
17. [CE2006/P2/Q46]
If Country X is more productive in producing every good than Country Y, then

options.A: the two countries may still trade with each other.
options.B: the gain from trade of Country X will be greater than that of Country Y.
options.C: Country X will have a lower opportunity cost in producing every good than Country Y.
options.D: no trade will take place between the two countries.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
18. [CE2007/P2/Q45]
Which of the following statements about international trade is correct if transportation cost increases?

options.A: The price of exported goods will increase if the exporting country has to bear the transportation costs.
options.B: The net gains from trade of the trading partners will remain unchanged as long as trade continues.
options.C: Comparative advantages will disappear if the transportation costs are higher than the total gains from trade.
options.D: Mutually beneficial trade is possible only if the transportation costs are lower than the total gains from trade.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
19. [CE2011/P2/Q47]
Country A is said to have a comparative advantage over Country B in producing good X when

options.A: Country A produces a greater amount of good X than Country B with all their resources
options.B: Country A gives up a smaller amount of other goods than Country B in producing 1 unit of good X
options.C: Country A's total output of good X is higher than Country B's total output of good X
options.D: Country A requires a greater amount of resources to produce 1 unit of good X than Country B

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
20. [DSESP/P1/Q37]
If Country X is more productive in producing every good than Country Y,

options.A: the gain from trade of Country X will be greater than that of Country Y.
options.B: mutually beneficial trade between the two countries is still possible.
options.C: Country Y will import every good from Country X instead of producing these goods by itself.
options.D: Country X may have a lower opportunity cost in producing every good than Country Y.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
21. [DSEPP/P1/Q39]
Assume both Country A and Country B produce and consume Good X and Good Y only. If Country A can produce a unit of Good X with less resources than Country B,
(1) Country A has an absolute advantage in producing Good X.
(2) Country A has a comparative advantage in producing Good X.
(3) Country B has an absolute advantage in producing Good Y.
(4) Country B has a comparative advantage in producing Good Y.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
22. [DSE2012/P1/Q38]
Consider the trade of a good between two countries. Suppose we know their opportunity costs of producing the good. Without knowing the terms of trade, we can determine
(1) the possible range of the terms of trade.
(2) the gain of each country from trading one unit of the good.
(3) the total gain of both countries from trading one unit of the good.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
23. [DSE2015/P1/Q41]
A country has an absolute advantage in producing good X. Which of the following statements about the country is correct?

options.A: The country can produce a greater amount of good X than another good with the same amount of resources.
options.B: The country has a comparative advantage in producing good X.
options.C: The country has an absolute disadvantage in producing another good.
options.D: The country may import good X from the international market.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
24. [DSE2026/P1/Q41]
A country has a comparative advantage in producing good X. Which of the following statements about the country is correct?

options.A: With the same amount of resources, it can produce more of good X than another good.
options.B: Its output of good X is higher than other countries.
options.C: It requires a smaller amount of resources to produce one unit of good X than other countries.
options.D: It gives up a smaller amount of another good than other countries in producing one unit of good X.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
1. [AL2008/P2/Q29]
Which of the following about Hong Kong's linked exchange rate system is INCORRECT?

options.A: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has to keep a great sum of foreign reserves.
options.B: There is no independent monetary policy in Hong Kong.
options.C: There will be an adverse effect on the real estate market in Hong Kong when the US keeps lowering the interest rate.
options.D: Hong Kong will experience imported inflation when the US Dollar continuously depreciates against the Renminbi.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
2. [CE1993/P2/Q33]
Which of the following about the linked exchange rate (聯繫匯率) in Hong Kong is correct?

options.A: It is determined by market forces.
options.B: It has been changed several times by the government.
options.C: The linked rate system is used to stabilize the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar.
options.D: It is an exchange rate between the Hong Kong dollar and a basket of foreign currencies.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
3. [CE1994/P2/Q45]
Which of the following statements about Hong Kong's note-issuing system is correct?

options.A: Any individual can exchange US dollars for Hong Kong dollars with the Monetary Authority at the rate US$1 = HK$7.8.
options.B: Hong Kong dollar notes are issued by the Monetary Authority.
options.C: Hong Kong dollars will always be fixed against the US dollar at the rate US$1 = HK$7.8 in the foreign exchange market.
options.D: To issue Hong Kong dollar notes, the note-issuing banks have to surrender US dollars to the Monetary Authority in exchange for certificates of indebtedness.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
4. [CE1996/P2/Q52]
Hong Kong practices a linked exchange rate system. In the foreign exchange market the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar relative to the US dollar is __________ and that relative to other currencies is __________.

options.B: fixed at US$1 = HK$7.8 … not fixed
options.D: not fixed … not fixed

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
5. [CE1998/P2/Q49]
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The exchange rate of the HK dollar relative to Renminbi is fixed.
options.B: The market exchange rate of the HK dollar relative to the US$ is fixed at US$1 = HK$7.8.
options.C: The competitiveness of Hong Kong exports decreases when the US dollar appreciates against other currencies.
options.D: Hong Kong will not have a balance of payments problem.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
6. [CE2000/P2/Q52]
Suppose the Japanese Yen appreciates greatly against the US dollar. Due to the linked exchange rate system,

options.A: the HK dollar will depreciate greatly against the Japanese Yen.
options.B: the US dollar will depreciate greatly against the Japanese Yen.
options.C: the US dollar will depreciate greatly against the euro.
options.D: the HK dollar will depreciate greatly against the euro.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
7. [CE2001/P2/Q46]
Under the linked exchange rate system in Hong Kong,

options.A: the market exchange rate of the HK dollar relative to the US dollar is fixed.
options.B: the market exchange rates of the HK dollar relative to currencies other than the US dollar are fixed.
options.C: The HK dollar will depreciate against the Australian dollar if the US dollar appreciates against the Australian dollar.
options.D: The HK dollar will appreciate against the Japanese yen if the US dollar appreciates against the Japanese yen.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
8. [CE2006/P2/Q47]
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The exchange rate of the Hong Kong Dollar (HKD) relative to the US dollar (USD) is fixed at USD1=HKD7.8 on the foreign exchange market.
options.B: If Mainland China has a visible trade surplus, Hong Kong will also have a visible trade surplus.
options.C: When the USD depreciates against the Euro, the HKD will also depreciate against the Euro.
options.D: All of the above.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
9. [CE2009/P2/Q50]
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong,

options.A: the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar with the US dollar in the foreign exchange market is fixed.
options.B: the Hong Kong government need not hold a large amount of foreign exchange reserves.
options.C: Hong Kong citizens can give the Hong Kong government Hong Kong dollars in exchange for US dollars at the linked rate.
options.D: the Hong Kong dollar banknotes are fully backed by foreign exchange reserves.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
10. [CE2011/P2/Q50]
Under the linked exchange rate system in Hong Kong,

options.A: the market exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar relative to the US dollar is fixed at US$1 = HK$7.8.
options.B: the three note-issuing banks in Hong Kong have the obligation to the general public to exchange Hong Kong dollars for US dollars at the linked rate.
options.C: the Hong Kong dollar banknotes do not have to be fully backed by foreign exchange reserves.
options.D: the market exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar relative to the Euro will move in the same direction as the market exchange rate of the US dollar relative to the Euro.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
11. [DSE2013/P1/Q40]
Which of the following statements about the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong is correct?
(1) Hong Kong dollar banknotes are fully backed by Renminbi and the US dollar.
(2) The Hong Kong Monetary Authority holds a considerable amount of foreign exchange reserves.
(3) All note-issuing banks can exchange for US dollars at the linked rate with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
(4) The exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar to the US dollar in the foreign exchange market is fixed.

options.D: (3) and (4) only

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
12. [DSE2015/P1/Q42]
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The money supply (M1) of Hong Kong has to be fully backed up by the US dollar.
options.B: The market exchange rate of the HK dollar to the US dollar is fixed at 1 USD to 7.8 HKD by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
options.C: Hong Kong's import volume will increase when the US dollar appreciates against other currencies.
options.D: A current account deficit in the US will lead to a current account deficit in Hong Kong.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
13. [DSE2017/P1/Q45]
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The non-bank public can sell their Hong Kong dollars to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in exchange for US dollars at any time.
options.B: It enables the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to carry out an expansionary monetary policy to stimulate private investment.
options.C: The market exchange rate of the US Dollar against the HK Dollar is fixed at US$1 = HK$7.8.
options.D: There would be a downward pressure on the consumer price indices of Hong Kong when the Renminbi continuously depreciates against the US Dollar.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
14. [DSE2020/P1/Q45]
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The money supply M1 of Hong Kong has to be fully backed up by the US dollar.
options.B: Hong Kong's export volume will increase when the US dollar depreciates against other currencies.
options.C: The market exchange rate of the HK dollar relative to the US dollar is fixed.
options.D: Hong Kong citizens can sell 1 USD to the three note-issuing banks for 7.8 HKD.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
15. [DSE2022/P1/Q45]
Which of the following statements about the Linked Exchange Rate System of Hong Kong is correct?

options.A: The public can sell their Hong Kong dollars to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in exchange for US dollars at the market exchange rate.
options.B: The public can sell their Hong Kong dollars to the three note-issuing banks in exchange for US dollars at the linked exchange rate.
options.C: An appreciation of Hong Kong dollar against Japanese yen would lead to an appreciation of US dollar against Japanese yen.
options.D: An appreciation of US dollar against Japanese yen would lead to an appreciation of Hong Kong dollar against Japanese yen.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
1. [CE1995/P2/Q40 [modified]]
Arrange the following assets in terms of liquidity in descending order:
(1) shares
(2) real estate
(3) bank notes
(4) demand deposits

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
2. [CE1996/P2/Q38]
Arrange the following bank assets in descending order of liquidity:
(1) loans and advances
(2) deposits with others banks
(3) real estates owned by the bank

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
3. [CE1997/P2/Q39 [modified]]
Holders of a/an ______ has the least risk and the highest liquidity.

options.D: savings deposit

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
4. [CE2004/P2/Q40 [modified]]
Which of the following kinds of assets has the lowest liquidity?

options.D: savings deposits

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
5. [CE2009/P2/Q35]
Which of the following assets has the highest liquidity?

options.D: time deposits

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
6. [CE2010/P2/Q37 [modified]]
Holders of ________ have the lowest liquidity.

options.D: real estates

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
7. [CE2011/P2/Q38]
Which of the following assets has the highest liquidity?

options.D: shares

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
8. [DSEPP/P1/Q29]
An asset which can be readily converted into cash at short notice without making a loss is regarded as a ___________ asset.

options.D: liquid

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
1. [CE1990/P2/Q32]
If Mr Wong transfers HK$100 from his savings account to his current account,

options.A: the total amount of bank deposits will increase.
options.B: The total money supply as measured by M1 will decrease.
options.C: The total money supply as measured by M2 will not change.
options.D: The total money supply as measured by M3 will increase.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
2. [CE1991/P2/Q34]
Which of the following is a component of Hong Kong’s money supply M2?

options.C: negotiable certificates of deposit held by banks
options.D: one-thousand-dollar gold coins issued by the Hong Kong government and held by banks

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
3. [CE1992/P2/Q32]
In Hong Kong, savings deposits with licensed banks are

options.B: included in the money supply M1.
options.C: included in the money supply M2.
options.D: included in the money supply M2, but excluded from the money supply M3.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
4. [CE1994/P2/Q43]
If an individual receives a cheque for $1000 from his friend and deposits it in his friend and deposits it in his savings account, Hong Kong’s money supply M1 will ______ and M2 will ______.

options.D: remain unchanged; remain unchanged

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
5. [CE1995/P2/Q43]
Mr Chan withdraws $600 000 from his savings deposit with a commercial bank and then deposits $500 000 with a restricted licence bank. The remaining $100 000 is kept at home. The immediate effect is that

options.D: M3 will increase by $500 000.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
6. [CE1996/P2/Q37]
Mr. Chan paid $200000 in cash to buy from Mr. Wong a certificate of deposit issued by a deposit-taking company. Mr. Wong then deposited this $200000 into his savings account. The immediate effects are
(1) M1 decrease by $200000.
(2) M2 remains unchanged.
(3) M3 increase by $200000.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
7. [CE1997/P2/Q36]
Which of the following will increase M1 in Hong Kong?

options.A: a repayment of HK$5 000 by cheque on a bank loan in Hong Kong
options.B: the lending of HK$5 000 in cash by a bank to a citizen in Hong Kong
options.C: a new deposit of HK$5 000 in a savings account with a bank in Hong Kong
options.D: a withdrawal of HK$5 000 in cash from a current account with a bank in Hong Kong

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
8. [CE1997/P2/Q37]
Suppose the money supply data of Hong Kong is as follows:
$ billion
Total issue of legal tender 3
Legal tender in circulation 2
Demand deposits 7
Deposits with licensed banks AND negotiable certificates of deposit issued by licensed banks 10 (other than those held by authorised institutions)
Deposits with restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies AND negotiable certificates of deposit issued by restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies (other 80 than those held by authorised institutions)
The money supply M2 is

options.D: $92 billion.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
9. [CE1998/P2/Q36]
Which of the following will cause an immediate change in the money supply M1 of Hong Kong?

options.A: You receive $500 cash from your father and deposit it in your current account.
options.B: You pay $4 000 cash to the landlord, who puts the money in his safe.
options.C: A fire burnt most of the banknotes kept in a bank.
options.D: You buy $10 000 worth of furniture with a cheque. The shop owner deposits it into his time deposit account.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
10. [CE1999/P2/Q39]
Suppose in a bank in Hong Kong, Mary withdraws HK$3 000 from her savings account and changes it for US dollars in cash. Which of the following statements about the Hong Kong dollar money supply is correct?

options.A: HK$M1 will increase while HK$M2 will remain unchanged.
options.B: HK$M1 will remain unchanged while HK$M3 will decrease.
options.C: Both HK$M1 and HK$M3 will remain unchanged.
options.D: Both HK$M1 and HK$M2 will decrease.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
11. [CE2000/P2/Q27]
Mr Wong withdraws $500 000 in cash from a deposit-taking company. He then deposits $300 000 with a bank as a time deposit and remits the remaining $200 000 overseas for the settlement of debts. Which of the following about the money supply M1 and M3 is correct?

options.A: Both M1 and M3 will increase.
options.B: Both M1 and M3 will decrease.
options.C: M1 will remain unchanged and M3 will decrease.
options.D: Both M1 and M3 will remain unchanged.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
12. [CE2000/P2/Q28]
Suppose the money supply of Hong Kong in a certain year was as follows:
$billion
Legal tender in circulation 10
Legal tender held by all deposit-taking institutions 2
Demand deposits with licensed banks 15
Savings and time deposits with licensed banks 60
Negotiable certificates of deposits issued by licensed banks and held by the public 25 Deposits with restricted licence banks and negotiable certificates of deposits issued by 32 restricted licence banks held by the public
The money supply M2 (in $ billion) was

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
13. [CE2001/P2/Q25]
In using the Easy Pay System (EPS) to settle a payment in exchange, an amount of money is immediately transferred from the buyer's bank account to the seller's. In response to an increase in EPS's service charge, some shops have stopped accepting payment by EPS.
Which of the following would be the immediate effect of the above change on the money supply M1 and M2?

options.A: Both M1 and M2 will increase.
options.B: M1 will increase and M2 will remain unchanged.
options.C: M1 will increase and M2 will decrease.
options.D: Both M1 and M2 will decrease.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
14. [CE2002/P2/Q33]
'Currency in public circulation' and 'savings deposits' are both included in Hong Kong's money supply
(1) M1.
(2) M2.
(3) M3.

options.D: (2) and (3) only

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
15. [CE2003/P2/Q32]
Mr Chan withdraws HK$50 000 from his savings account with a bank in Hong Kong and remits HK$40 000 through a bank to the U.K. He changes the remaining HK$10 000 into the newly issued HK$10 notes and puts them into his safety deposit box in a bank.
Which of the following would be the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

options.A: Both the HK$ M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$40 000.
options.B: HK$ M1 will increase by HK$10 000 while HK$ M2 will decrease by HK$50 000.
options.C: HK$ M2 will decrease by HK$50 000 while HK$ M3 will remain unchanged.
options.D: HK$ M1 will remain unchanged while HK$ M2 will decrease by HK$40 000.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
16. [CE2004/P2/Q37]
Which of the following would decrease the money supply M2 in Hong Kong?

options.A: Mr Au repays a HK$10 000 loan in cash to a licensed bank in Hong Kong.
options.B: Mr Bean withdraws HK$20 000 from a savings account with a licensed bank in Hong Kong and holds it as cash.
options.C: Mr Chan transfers HK$30 000 from his savings account to his current account with a licensed bank in Hong Kong.
options.D: Mr Ding withdraws HK$40 000 from his time deposit in a restricted licence bank in Hong Kong and remits the money overseas.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
17. [CE2005/P2/Q38]
Suppose Mrs Wong withdraws HK$300 000 from her savings deposit with a commercial bank. She converts HK$200 000 of the above amount into Renminbi (人民幣) and deposits it into a Renminbi savings deposit with the same bank. She keeps the remaining HK$100 000 at home. The immediate effect of the above events is:

options.A: Hong Kong dollar money supply M1 would increase by $100 000.
options.B: Hong Kong dollar money supply M2 would decrease by $300 000.
options.C: Hong Kong dollar money supply M2 would remain unchanged.
options.D: Hong Kong dollar money supply M3 would increase by $100 000.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
18. [CE2006/P2/Q35]
Mr Chan withdraws HK$20 000 from his deposit in a restricted licence bank in Hong Kong. He later puts HK$15 000 as time deposit in a licensed bank in Hong Kong and holds the remaining HK$5 000 as cash. The immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply would be:

options.B: Both M1 and M2 remain unchanged.
options.C: M1 increases while M2 remains unchanged.
options.D: M1 increases while M3 remains unchanged.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
19. [CE2007/P2/Q39]
If an individual deposits $600 000 cash into a time deposit account with a deposit-taking company, Hong Kong's money supply M1 will ______ and M2 will ______.

options.D: increase ... increase

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
20. [CE2008/P2/Q37]
Suppose, after making a series of unsuccessful add-value transactions through EPS in which their bank accounts were debited, more Octopus cardholders use cash to make their add-value transactions. This would immediately increase

options.C: the amount of savings deposits of banks.
options.D: the amount of time deposits of banks.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
21. [CE2010/P2/Q39]
Grace receives a remittance of HK$530 000 from overseas. She saves HK$500 000 of the total amount as time deposits in a restricted licence bank and the rest as demand deposits in a licensed bank. What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the money supply of Hong Kong?

options.A: M1 will increase by HK$30 000 and M2 will increase by HK$530 000.
options.B: M1 will increase by HK$30 000 and M3 will increase by HK$500 000.
options.C: M2 will increase by HK$30 000 and M3 will increase by HK$500 000.
options.D: M2 will increase by HK$30 000 and M3 will increase by HK$530 000.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
22. [CE2011/P2/Q40]
Which of the following transactions in Hong Kong would reduce the money supply M2 of Hong Kong?

options.A: Mr Chan withdraws $7 000 from his savings account with a licensed bank and holds it as cash.
options.B: Mr Lee transfers $100 000 from his current account to his savings account with a licensed bank.
options.C: Miss Wong transfers $500 000 from her time deposit account with a licensed bank to her time deposit account with a restricted licence bank.
options.D: Miss Cheung deposits $6 000 cash into her time deposit account with a licensed bank.

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
23. [DSESP/P1/Q29]
Mr Chan withdraws HK$4 000 000 from his deposit account in a restricted licence bank in Hong Kong. He then puts HK$3 500 000 as time deposit in a licensed bank in Hong Kong and holds the remaining HK$500 000 as cash.
The immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply would be:

options.A: Both M2 and M3 remain unchanged.
options.B: M1 increases while M2 remains unchanged.
options.C: M2 increases while M3 remains unchanged.
options.D: M2 increases while M3 decreases.

17. [CE2001/P2/Q12]
Dennis opened a convenience store and he has employed his friend, John, as a storekeeper. Dennis' work is classified as ______ and John's work is classified as ______.

options.D: entrepreneurship ... tertiary production

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
18. [CE2002/P2/Q15]
In economics, which of the following statements about capital is correct?

options.A: The quantity of fixed capital cannot be changed in the short run.
options.B: Capital earns the highest rate of return among all factors of production.
options.C: Capital is produced to satisfy consumers' wants directly.
options.D: The geographical mobility of capital is greater than that of land.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
19. [CE2003/P2/Q16]
Which of the following statements about ‘land’ is correct?

options.A: The supply of land may be increased through human effort.
options.B: The supply of land may change over time.
options.C: Land is a free good because it is part of nature.
options.D: Land is a scarce good because it cannot be produced.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
20. [CE2004/P2/Q14]
Michael Owen is a famous football player for Liverpool Football Club. In economics, he provides the service of ______ and he engages in ______ production.

options.D: labour ... tertiary

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
21. [CE2005/P2/Q15]
Which of the following is classified as land in economics?

options.A: soil with chemical fertilizers added to it
options.D: a piece of cultivated land

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
22. [CE2006/P2/Q13]
Mr Chan is the owner of a printing factory and he employs Mary as an accountant. The factory engages in ______ production and Mary provides the service of the factor ________.

options.D: tertiary ... entrepreneurship

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
23. [CE2007/P2/Q16]
Which of the following statements about land is correct?

options.A: Crude oil unextracted is land because it is fixed in supply.
options.B: Ocean is land because it is geographically immobile.
options.C: Rainfall on a piece of farmland is land because it is a gift of nature for production.
options.D: Wood being cut in the tropical forest is land because it is used for production.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
24. [CE2007/P2/Q17]
Land is different from capital in that

options.A: the supply of land cannot be controlled, whereas that of capital can be.
options.B: land is a free good but capital is an economic good.
options.C: land has a lower occupational mobility than capital.
options.D: land has a greater supply elasticity than capital.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
25. [CE2007/P2/Q18]
In Economics, a taxi is classified as _______ and the income of the taxi owner from renting the taxi to a driver is classified as _______.

options.D: capital ... profit

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
26. [CE2008/P2/Q14]
Which of the following are land in economics?
(1) the Chinese white dolphins living in the waters around Lantau Island
(2) the giant pandas living in Ocean Park Hong Kong
(3) migratory birds found in the Deep Bay (后海灣)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
27. [CE2009/P2/Q15]
Which of the following belongs to the factor of production 'land'?

options.A: endangered species of Tibetan antelope (藏羚羊) found on the Tibetan Plateau (青藏高原)
options.B: flowers planted in Hong Kong Disneyland
options.C: crocodiles living in Hong Kong Wetland Park
options.D: oxygen provided in the trains running across the Tibetan Plateau

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
28. [CE2010/P2/Q17]
Which of the following about ‘land’ and ‘capital’ is correct?

options.A: Both land and capital can be increased by human effort.
options.B: Both land and capital are fixed factors of production.
options.C: Land is more elastic in supply than capital.
options.D: Land is less geographically mobile than capital.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
29. [CE2011/P2/Q16]
In economics, a medical doctor in the public hospital provides the service of ________ and he engages in ________ production.

options.D: labour ... tertiary

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
30. [CE2011/P2/Q17]
Miss Chan rents a studio to record songs. In economics, the studio is classified as ________ and the rental income of the studio owner is classified as ________.

options.D: capital ... interest

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
31. [DSE2016/P1/Q6]
A school is a production unit which provides educational services. The following are people and objects that are usually found at a school:
(1) the school building
(2) teachers
(3) students
(4) private cars owned by teachers
(5) sanitisers（洗手液）in the toilets
Which of the above items are capital of the school?

options.D: (1), (4) and (5) only

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
32. [DSE2019/P1/Q8]
Which of the following are capital of a cafe?
(1) coffee machines
(2) coffee beans
(3) video game consoles brought by its customers for party
(4) comic books which can be borrowed by its customers free of charge

options.D: (2), (3) and (4) only

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
33. [DSE2020/P1/Q6]
Refer to the following dialogue.
Given the return of land is rent, the return of labour is wage, the return of capital is interest while the return of entrepreneur is profit. The income earned by Captain Cook consists of ______ while the remaining income earned by Landlord Li consists of ______.
[See diagram in original PDF]

options.D: wage and interest ...rent and profit

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
1. [DSESP/P1/Q10]
Peter Pang is an indigenous male resident in the New Territories. Which of the following are guided by price signals?
(1) He buys a concessionary house (丁屋) from his cousin.
(2) He is given a red packet by the Indigenous Inhabitant Representative (原居民代表) during the Lunar New Year.
(3) He rents one of his concessionary houses to a tenant who is not an indigenous resident.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
2. [DSE2017/P1/Q12]
A famous artist, Tsz-Wah, held a show. Many people complained that they could not buy a ticket. Ticket touts resold the tickets on the Internet and some buyers paid a price higher than HK$10 000 for a ticket. The above case illustrates the ______ function of price because ______.

options.A: rationing ... the tickets are rationed to the highest-valued buyers
options.B: rationing ... demand will be reduced by a higher price
options.C: allocative ... more profits can be earned with a higher price
options.D: allocative ... more resources should be allocated to the producer to raise the supply

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
3. [DSE2020/P1/Q13]
In recent years, the rise in demand for private cars in China has attracted Volkswagen, a German car manufacturer, to set up car manufacturing factories in China.
The above case illustrates the __________ function of price because __________.

options.A: rationing ... private cars are sold to the highest-valued users in China
options.B: rationing ... fewer buyers are willing to buy private cars in Germany
options.C: allocative ... the supply of private cars falls in Germany
options.D: allocative ... more resources are allocated to the production of private cars in China

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
4. [DSE2022/P1/Q10]
In 2021, Trial & Error (試當真), a Hong Kong YouTube channel, held its first live show. The following was the pricing arrangement of its tickets.
Ticket price adjusts daily at 10 am.
Date Ticket price
9 August $10 000
10 August $5 000
11 August $2 000
... ...
31 August $20
1 September $10
onwards
The above case illustrates the __________ function of price because _______________.

options.A: allocative ... more resources can be allocated to the production of the show
options.B: allocative ... the arrangement can guarantee a sell-out of the tickets
options.C: rationing ... the tickets are sold to the highest-valued buyers
options.D: rationing ... the tickets are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
1. [CE1990/P2/Q9]
The ban on the ivory trade in general harms the ______ craftsmen most because of their relatively ______ ______ mobility.

options.D: older, high, geographical

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
2. [CE1991/P2/Q6]
Suppose the government provides housing subsidies to teachers serving in the same school for over 10 years. Such a measure will tend to ____ the occupational mobility and ____ the geographical mobility of these teachers.

options.D: decrease, increase

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
3. [CE1992/P2/Q9]
Which of the following can increase the occupational mobility of labour?

options.A: the development of industries requiring high technology
options.B: the setting up of more professional associations
options.C: the expansion of vocational training courses
options.D: the extension of the Mass Transit Railway network

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
4. [CE1993/P2/Q14]
Lawyers generally have a low occupational mobility because

options.B: they are not skilful in other professions.
options.C: they have high opportunity cost in changing jobs.
options.D: they are members of the Hong Kong Law Society.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
5. [CE1995/P2/Q21]
Which of the following will raise the occupational mobility of labour?
(1) a higher degree of specialization of skills
(2) more information about job vacancies
(3) greater power of labour unions
(4) provision of retraining programmes

options.D: (3) and (4) only

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
6. [CE1997/P2/Q14]
Which of the following has the least occupational mobility?

options.D: dental surgeon

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
7. [CE1999/P2/Q16]
Which of the following types of people is more occupationally mobile?

options.A: professors in economics in a university
options.D: company secretaries

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
8. [CE2001/P2/Q14]
Suppose the government starts to recruit experienced Putunghua teachers from Mainland China. This would ______ the ______ mobility of experienced Putunghua teachers in Mainland China.

options.D: increase ... geographical

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
9. [CE2004/P2/Q15]
In order to attract more Mainland professionals to work in Hong Kong, some firms plan to provide a housing allowance for them. This would ______ the ______ of these Mainland professionals.

options.D: increase ... geographical mobility

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
10. [CE2006/P2/Q15]
When division of labour is practised, workers will have a ______ occupational mobility because ______.

options.A: higher ... the labour productivity is raised
options.B: higher ... the capital goods are used more fully
options.C: lower ... work becomes dull and monotonous
options.D: lower ... workers are only trained for a particular skill

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
11. [CE2008/P2/Q15]
In which of the following situations will the occupational mobility of labour increase?

options.B: tightened restrictions on obtaining a professional licence
options.D: raising the legal retirement age

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
12. [DSE2012/P1/Q5]
The occupational mobility of labour in an economy will increase when

options.A: the cross-border railway network is improved.
options.B: licences are required for more types of job in the labour market.
options.C: tax allowances are provided for continuing education.
options.D: there is a greater degree of specialisation in production.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
13. [DSE2014/P1/Q11]
Which of the following would most likely increase the occupational mobility of labour in an economy?

options.A: The labour unions have stronger bargaining power for the welfare of their members.
options.B: The labour department provides tuition fee rebates for participants of retraining programmes.
options.C: The transport network is improved by the extension of highways.
options.D: The government stops granting funding for an online data system about job vacancies.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
14. [DSE2015/P1/Q4]
The __________ mobility of labour will decrease if __________.

options.A: geographical ... the government introduces “city-bike rental scheme” in all train stations
options.B: geographical ... several big companies set up child care centres in their offices
options.C: occupational ... the travelling subsidy provided by the government is reduced due to a budget deficit
options.D: occupational ... licences are required by the government for more professions

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
15. [DSE2016/P1/Q9]
Which of the following is the most mobile in terms of occupational mobility?

options.C: a graduate trainee in a law firm
options.D: a clerk in an accounting firm

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
16. [DSE2019/P1/Q6]
In the 2018-19 Budget, the Hong Kong Government raised the subsidy ceiling of the Continuing Education Fund from $10000 to $20000 per applicant to encourage members of the public to pursue further education. This policy will lead to a rise in ______ and ______ in the future.

options.D: labour productivity ... occupational mobility

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
17. [DSE2022/P1/Q8]
The __________ of labour in Hong Kong will increase if _______________.

options.A: occupational mobility ... a professional labour union tightens the requirements for entering the industry
options.B: occupational mobility ... the Government waives the examination for foreign-trained doctors to work in Hong Kong
options.C: geographical mobility ... Tuen Ma Line connecting Tuen Mun and Ma On Shan is open
options.D: geographical mobility ... the Government reduces the travel subsidy to the low-income group

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
18. [DSE2023/P1/Q7]
The occupational mobility of labour of an economy will decrease if

options.A: transport subsidies are provided to workers who live in remote districts.
options.C: the statutory retirement age is raised from 65 to 70.
options.D: more job retraining courses are provided by the government free of charge.

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
19. [DSE2026/P1/Q11]
Which of the following will increase the geographical mobility of labour in a country?
(1) The government increases the amount of travelling subsidies to workers.
(2) The government increases the subsidies on retraining programmes.
(3) Foreign workers are required to apply for an additional visa to work in that country.

options.D: (2) and (3) only

questions.text:

options.D: the emigration of skilled workers

questions.text:

Which of the following can increase the productivity of factory workers?
(1) abandoning the piece-rate system
(2) installing more machinery
(3) importing labour from Mainland China
(4) providing a better working environment

options.D: (3) and (4) only

questions.text:
3. [CE1993/P2/Q6]
Which of the following will improve the average productivity of labour in an economy?
(1) extending compulsory education to a higher level
(2) raising the retirement age
(3) increasing the quantity of capital goods
(4) raising unemployment benefits

options.D: (2) and (4) only

questions.text:

Year 1991 1992
Number of workers employed 20 25
Units of dresses produced 90 80 000
000

questions.text:
8. [CE1997/P2/Q55]
An increase in the number of Form 7 graduates studying in the universities will result in

questions.text:

(1) there is an increase in the number of machines.

options.D: (3) and (4) only

options.D: The banking system will be less able to create deposits.

A higher average labour productivity means a higher

Country A Country B

options.D: (3) and (4) only

- equilibrium quantity decreases Q => Q’

(b)(ii)
[Answer diagram in the original PDF.]
- demand for U.S. car manufacturing workers increases / demand curve shifts to the right

- employment of U.S. car manufacturing workers increases L1 => L2

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Research shows that the "Individual Visit Scheme" of mainland tourists has brought economic benefits to Hong Kong.
However, more and more Hong Kong residents have called on the government to reduce the number of mainland
tourists to Hong Kong under the Scheme.
(d) Some residents complained that the large number of tourists overloaded the public transportation system,
resulting in a large increase in travel time for all passengers. Explain, in terms of externality, why
inefficiency may exist when the transportation system is overcrowded. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
(d) Negative externality / divergence between private and social costs. (1)
When the public transportation system is overcrowded (i.e., at full capacity), any additional passenger using
the system would increase the time cost for other passengers without having to compensate them for this extra
cost (implying a divergence between private and social costs). As marginal social cost is now higher than
marginal social benefit, the number of passengers using the system would exceed its efficient level. (3)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
These years many customers like to take photos of the food they have in restaurants and share them on social media.
However, some high-end restaurants do not allow their customers to take photos. Explain how the "photo-taking-and-
sharing" behaviour of the customers may involve externality. (3 marks)
questions.solution:
Taking photos may disturb other people in the restaurants/sharing the photos in the social media may disclose
the design of dishes. Both possibilities may have an undesirable effect on the revenue/profit of the restaurants,
but such effects are not compensated (financially or otherwise) by the photo-takers. Such photo-taking-and
sharing behaviour may thus involve negative externality (external cost is involved). (3)
or
Taking photos and sharing them in social media may have a promotion effect, attracting more customers—
bringing higher revenue/profit—to the restaurant, but the photo takers do not receive compensation for such
benefits. Such photo-taking-and sharing behaviour may thus involve positive externality (external benefit is
involved). (3)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Pokémon Go is a popular game for which gamers need to move around different places with their smartphones to
catch the cyber-pets. Its developer has placed hotspots in different areas where many gamers are attracted to gather.
Some restaurants in remote areas found their business sharply increased as they are located near these hotspots.
(a) Based on the above information, explain, in terms of externality, how the placing of the hotspots may result
in inefficiency. (3 marks)
(b) How may such a problem of inefficiency be relieved by market? (2 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) Positive externality. Restaurants in remote areas enjoy benefits from increased business due to the game
developer’s choice of hotspots locations without paying the developer. So external benefit exists and marginal
social benefit is greater than marginal social cost. The number of existing hotspots near the restaurants is
lower than that required by the efficiency level. (3)
(b) The restaurants may pay the game developer to increase the hotspots nearby. (2)
Or
The game developer may charge the restaurants for placing more hotspots near them. (2)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Getting vaccinated is an effective way to prevent infection and protect oneself from flu viruses. Using the concept of
externality, explain why the government provision of subsidy on Seasonal Influenza Vaccination (接 種 節
季 性流感疫
苗) may improve economic efficiency. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
Getting vaccinated protects oneself as well as lowering the chance of others being infected by flu. Since the
person receiving vaccination is not compensated by others (whose chances of being infected are reduced),
there exists external benefit, with marginal social benefit exceeding marginal social cost. This implies that the
number of people getting vaccinated is below the efficient level. Subsidy can increase the quantity of
vaccination towards the efficient level and thus narrow the gap between marginal social benefit and marginal
social cost. (4)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Masks have become a daily necessity as it is compulsory for people to wear masks in many public areas.
(d) Wearing surgical mask can reduce the chance of contracting diseases for an individual and can prevent
spreading diseases to others as well. In terms of externality, explain how the subsidy could improve
economic efficiency. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
(d) Wearing mask protects oneself as well as lowering the chance of others being infected. Since the person
wearing mask is not compensated by others (whose chances of being infected are reduced), there exists
external benefit, with marginal social benefit exceeding marginal social cost. This implies that the number of
people wearing mask is below the efficient level i.e. under-consumption of masks. Subsidy can increase the
number of people wearing mask towards the efficient level (by lowering the marginal private cost), and thus
narrow the gap between marginal social benefit and marginal social cost. (4)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Many industrial activities emit carbon dioxide, intensifying global warming and potentially bringing hazards to all
human beings.
(a) In terms of externality, explain why the emission of carbon dioxide by industrial activities may result in
economic inefficiency. (4 marks)
(b) Explain how the introduction of the system of carbon credits may improve economic efficiency. (2 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) Negative externality may be involved when producers engaged in industrial activities which emit carbon
dioxide do not have to pay compensation for the harm inflicted on others. (2)
As a result, equilibrium output determined by equality between marginal private (= social) benefit and
marginal private (< social) cost would be higher than the socially efficient level (where marginal social benefit
= marginal social cost). Such overproduction resulting from the divergence between marginal private cost and
marginal social cost implies economic inefficiency (i.e., inefficient allocation of the society's resources in
producing such products). (2)
(b) Payment for carbon credits to engage in production activities that emit carbon dioxide would raise the
producers' marginal private cost and thus lower equilibrium output towards the efficient level. At this lower
level of output, the gap between marginal private cost and marginal social cost is reduced and economic
efficiency is improved. (2)

隧
Source C: An extract of a report on traffic congestion
Traffic congestion not only affects individual drivers, but also results in inconvenience to society as a whole. Apart
from the time wasted during congestion, people also need to allow extra time for the journey to cater for the uncertainty
in travelling time. The stop-and-go traffic pattern during congestion increases the total operating costs of vehicles as
more fuel would be consumed.
Refer to Source C.
(c)(i) Explain, with ONE example, why there may be a divergence between private and social costs during
traffic congestion. (3 marks)
(c)(ii) Explain why the situation in part (i) may result in inefficiency. (2 marks)
questions.solution:
(c)(i) | The drivers using the tunnel would have adverse effects on other drivers without paying compensation to
the parties being affected. These adverse effects can be viewed as an external cost, which the drivers
would not consider when making their driving decisions.
The example of external cost includes extra time for journey to cater for uncertainty/extra operating cost
in the stop-and-go traffic.
(3)
(c)(ii) The above case implies that marginal social cost is larger than marginal social benefit. The tunnel is 'over-

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
The Olympic Games attract billions of international television viewers to watch the competitions among thousands of
top athletes.
(a) Some restaurants in shopping malls find their businesses increase sharply when the malls broadcast
Olympic events. Explain how the broadcast of Olympic events may result in a divergence between private
and social benefits. (3 marks)
(b) Suppose the divergence in part (a) does exist. How can market mechanism help reduce this divergence?
(2 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) The broadcast would attract more customers and thus bring more business to the restaurants. However, in the
absence of compensations from these restaurants (beneficiaries) to the shopping malls (benefactors) for
broadcasting the Olympic Games, there would exist a positive externality (or external benefit), with the
marginal social benefit (MSB) from the broadcast exceeding the marginal private benefit (MPB). (3)
(b) The difference between MSB and MPB implies under-provision of broadcast. A market solution may involve
the restaurants paying the malls to broadcast more games so that the number of Olympic events broadcast
would increase towards its efficient level. (2)

imported from Country C. (6 marks)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
The declining labour force would be one of the problems of Hong Kong in the future.
Source: Highlight of a report on manpower to the Legislative Council
 To relieve manpower shortage and to supplement skills not readily available in the market, local employers
can import workers through different schemes.
 For higher-skilled professionals, the annual number of imported professionals (via different schemes) was
67 656 in 2018.
 For lower-skilled workers, employers can import them through the Supplementary Labour Scheme (SLS).
Under this scheme, restrictions are placed to protect the local workers. For example, wages of imported
workers cannot be lower than the median wage of local workers in such positions.
 Total number of imported workers under SLS was 3 225 in 2018 and a high portion of them worked in
elderly care service industry.
 - Despite the importation of workers, there were still unfilled vacancies of 2 630 in elderly care service
industry.
(e) Suppose the Government has two strategies to address the problem of declining labour force.
Strategy I: Providing extra childcare service and cash to parents in order to increase the birth rate
Strategy II: Expanding the existing schemes in order to import more workers
With reference to the Source and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss the effects of each strategy on
average labour productivity
questions.solution:
(e) Average labour productivity:
Strategy I:
In the short term, newborn babies and children are not yet ready to join the labour force, so that they would not
affect labour productivity.
In the long term, labour productivity depends crucially on the education and training of the new, younger
generations relative to the older generations. For families with limited resources, an increase in the number of
children means that each child can only get a smaller share of such resources, including parental care and
education. Average labour productivity would fall as a result, unless the government is willing to invest more
and more in education to improve the knowledge and skills of the new generation over time.
Strategy II:
It depends on the ratio of high-skilled workers to low-skilled workers. According to Source D, for imported
workers, the numerator was much bigger than the denominator. Labour productivity would rise when the
proportion of high-skilled imported workers exceeds the proportion of high-skilled local workers.
Evaluation:
Strategy II may be better than Strategy I in raising labour productivity as the government could simply choose
to import more high-skilled workers.

unchanged.’ Explain Ann’s output decision with reference to the profit-maximising condition under perfect
competition. (3 marks)

last unit equals its marginal revenue (i.e., the market price). (1)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Many countries have considered imposing ‘soft drink tax’ for health reasons. Suppose a country decides to impose a
per unit tax on the sellers for every bottle of soft drink sold in the market.
(c) ‘As the amount of tax imposed on each bottle is the same irrespective of the bottle size, the proportion of
larger-bottle soft drinks sold in the market will increase.’ Explain this argument using the law of demand.
(5 marks)
questions.solution:
(c) Law of demand: when the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded of the good decreases, vice versa,
ceteris paribus. Here the unit of measurement to which the tax applies is “bottle,” rather than volume (e.g., in
litres), of soft drinks. When the same amount of tax is added to each unit (bottle), then -- per volume of liquid
contained -- larger-bottle soft drinks would become cheaper than the small-bottle ones. The relative price of
larger-bottle soft drinks (in terms of small-bottle ones) thus drops. The law of demand then implies that people
would buy more larger-bottle soft drinks relative to small-bottle ones, so the proportion of larger-bottle soft
drinks sold in the market would increase. (5)

take long-distance flights, increasing the average flight distance. (4)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
Each year, during the tourism peak season of the National Day golden week in October, a large number of tourists
from Mainland China visit Hong Kong.
Many of these tourists stay at local 3-star hotels. Assume that the room charges of these hotels are the same at
the same points in time.
(a)(i) Every September these hotels have vacant rooms. Draw a supply-demand diagram in Figure 2 for this
situation. Explain your answer. (3 marks)
(a)(ii) As compared to September, these hotels have fewer vacant rooms during the National Day golden week in
October even though they raise their room charges during this week.
Indicate the above changes in the supply-demand situation of these hotel rooms in Figure 2. Explain your
answer. (6 marks)
questions.solution:
[Answer diagram in the original PDF.]
(a)(i)
Diagram:
- Sept. price > equilibrium price (1)
- ab = excess supply in Sept. (1)
Verbal Elaboration:
- initial excess supply in Sept. (1)
(a)(ii) Diagram:
- demand curve shifts to the right to position D’D’ in the golden week (1)
- price raised to a new level (there is an excess supply at the new price) (1)
- excess supply in the golden week = a’b’ (1)
- a’b’ < ab (1)
Verbal Elaboration:
- an increase in demand (1)
- smaller excess supply in the golden week (1)

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
The declining labour force would be one of the problems of Hong Kong in the future.
Source D: Highlight of a report on manpower to the Legislative Council
- To relieve manpower shortage and to supplement skills not readily available in the market, local employers can
import workers through different schemes.
- For higher-skilled professionals, the annual number of imported professionals (via different schemes) was 67 656
in 2018.
- For lower-skilled workers, employers can import them through the Supplementary Labour Scheme (SLS). Under
this scheme, restrictions are placed to protect the local workers. For example, wages of imported workers cannot
be lower than the median wage of local workers in such positions.
- Total number of imported workers under SLS was 3 225 in 2018 and a high portion of them worked in elderly
care service industry.
- Despite the importation of workers, there were still unfilled vacancies of 2 630 in elderly care service industry.
(c) Refer to Source D. With the aid of a supply-demand diagram, explain the phenomenon ‘despite the
importation of workers, there were still vacancies in elderly care service industry’. (7 marks)
questions.solution:
(c) Verbal elaboration:
Initially wage rate is below its equilibrium (market-clearing) level, so shortage or excess demand for labour
arises. Importation of workers would increase labour supply, but not enough to eliminate the shortage. Though
fewer than before, vacancies (excess demand) would still exist. (3)
Illustrate in the diagram:
- correct position of W (1) ₀
- correct position of initial excess demand (ex dd ) (1) ₀
- rightward shift of supply curve (1)
- a smaller excess demand (ex dd ) (1) ₁
[Answer diagram in the original PDF.]

questions.text:

(∵ trucks and private cars are related products but not necessarily competing / different lines of vehicle
production.)
(1+1)
Motives:

- make use of brand name
- economies of scale
(Mark the FIRST TWO points only.)

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Micro
questions.text:
A television broadcasting company takes over a film production company. Give TWO possible economic motives of
the takeover. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
Vertical (backward) integration.
(∵ the television company takes over a film production company at an earlier stage of production.)
TWO possible economic motives:
- to guarantee a stable source of films to be shown on the television
- the television company is able to direct or influence the kind of films to be shot by the film company
- economies of scale, e.g. the expertise, equipment and plants of the television company can be more fully
utilized
- to diversify the television company's risk of investment
- any other relevant point
(Mark the FIRST TWO points only.)
@2; max: 4

questions.text:

motives for this type of integration. (5 marks)

(1)

- financial economy of scale
- managerial economy of scale
- marketing economy of scale

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
(a) Give ONE reason to explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping. (3 marks)
(b) Suppose there is an increase in the price of raw materials. With reference to the market adjustment
mechanism from the short run equilibrium to the long run equilibrium, explain the long run effect of the
above change on the price level with the aid of Figure 1. (9 marks)
[Diagram / picture here — kept so it can be redrawn in Python later. See the original PDF.]
questions.solution:
(a) Wealth effect: As many of the assets in the economy are denominated in nominal values, the higher the price
level, the lower the purchasing power of money. This reduces the wealth of the economy (in real terms). As a
result, households and firms reduce their purchases of all goods and services and the real output drops.
Interest rate effect: As the price level rises, households and firms demand more money to finance their
transactions. Given the fixed supply of money, the interest rate would rise. An increase in interest rate would
cause decline in investment and consumption and also the real output.
Net exports effect: As the domestic price level rises, foreign-made goods become relatively cheaper so the
quantity demanded of imports increases. However, the rise in the domestic price level also means that
domestic-made goods are relatively more expensive to foreign buyers so the quantity demanded of exports
decreases. When the volumes of exports decrease and of imports increase, net exports will decrease (if the
price-elasticities of demand for exports and/or imports are sufficiently high). Because net exports are a
component of real GDP, the demand for real GDP declines as net exports decline.
Any one max: 3
(b) Verbal elaboration:
Increase in the price of raw materials results in a rise in factor prices. So the SRAS will decrease. Price level
increases and the output will fall in the short run. The resulting excess supply of labour / deflationary (output)
gap will result in a downward pressure on the input prices. In the long run, wages will adjust downward and
the SRAS will increase and the price level will fall back to the original level. (5)
[Answer diagram in the original PDF.]
Indicate on the diagram:
- SRAS shifts to the left (1)
- P increases, Y drops (1)
- SRAS shifts back to the original position (1)
- final fall in P, back to the original level (1)

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text: Explain, with ONE reason, why the short-run aggregate supply curve is upward-sloping. (3 marks)
questions.solution:
When the price level increases, the adjustment of input prices is imperfect/incomplete (e.g. due to the long
term contracts of factor of production), so the real cost of production —i.e. nominal cost divided by the
general price level—will fall. Firms would thus use more factor inputs to produce larger output. Therefore, the
SRAS curve is upward-sloping, i.e. a higher price level would result in a higher output level. (3)

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
Figure 2 shows the aggregate demand (AD), short run aggregate supply (SRAS) and long run aggregate supply
(LRAS) curves of an economy.
[Diagram / picture here — kept so it can be redrawn in Python later. See the original PDF.]
(a) Give ONE reason to explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping. (3 marks)
(b) Suppose the economy initially operates at E0. With the aid of Figure 2, explain how the market adjustment
mechanism can restore the aggregate output to the full-employment output level in the long run. (5 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) Reasons:
- Wealth effect: As many of the assets in the economy are denominated in nominal values, the higher the
price level, the lower the purchasing power of these monetary assets. This reduces the wealth of the
economy (in real terms). As a result, consumption decreases and the aggregate quantity of output
demanded drops.
- Interest rate effect: As the price level rises, households and firms demand more money to finance their
transactions. Given the fixed supply of money, the interest rate would rise. An increase in interest rate
would cause a decline in investment and consumption and thus the aggregate quantity of output
demanded.
- Net exports effect: As the domestic price level rises, foreign-made goods become relatively cheaper so the
quantity demanded of imports increases. The rise in the domestic price level also means that domestically
produced goods are relatively more expensive to foreign buyers, so the quantity demanded of exports
decreases. When the volume of exports decreases and that of imports increases, net exports will decrease
(if the price elasticities of demand for exports and/or imports are sufficiently high). As net exports are a
component of aggregate expenditure, the aggregate quantity of output demanded would drop as net
exports decline.
@3; max: 3
[Mark the FIRST point ONLY.]
(b) Verbal elaboration:
The economy is facing a deflationary (output) gap. (1)
There is an excess supply in the factor market. (1)
It creates pressure for factor prices to adjust downward. Costs of production would drop. (1)
Short run aggregate supply (SRAS) would increase over time, thus restoring output level to the full-
employment output level, $Y_{f}$, in the long run. (1)
Indicate in the diagram:
- Rightward shift of short run aggregate supply curve, reaching $Y_{f}$. (1)

strategy on the US economy in terms of trade balance.

(d) Effects on trade balance:
Strategy I (raising the salaries tax rate for the high-income group):
- As disposable income decreases, consumption, including the consumption of imported goods, decreases.
Imports decrease. Given that the value of exports remains unchanged, trade balance of the US will
improve.

unchanged, prices of US products would decrease relative to goods produced in other countries. US
exports tend to increase and US imports tend to decrease, thus improving the trade balance of the US.
Strategy II (cancelling the tariffs on Chinese imports):
- Cancellation of tariffs on imports from China would lower prices of those goods and thus increase the
volume of imports from China. Given that the value of exports remains unchanged, the trade balance of
the US will be worsened.
- - As prices of imported raw materials from China decrease, costs of production decrease. SRAS increases.
Price level decreases. Assuming that prices of other countries' products remain unchanged, prices of US
products would decrease relative to goods produced in other countries. US exports tend to increase and
US imports tend to decrease, thus improving the trade balance of the US.

questions.text:

Suppose the closing down of many companies leads to a sharp decrease in demand for loans. As a result, some
banks cannot lend out their excess reserves.
(b)(i) Explain how the decrease in demand for loans would affect the opportunity cost to these banks of holding
excess reserves. (4 marks)
(b)(ii) Using the process of deposit creation, explain how a decrease in demand for loans could affect the deposit
creation ability of the banking system. (4 marks)
(c) Suppose the banking system has an excess reserve of $50 million and its balance sheet is as follows:
Assets ($m) | Liabilities ($m)
Reserves | 250 Deposits | 1 000
Loans | 750
What is the maximum possible amount of total deposits in the banking system if no banks hold excess
reserves? Show your workings. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
(b)(i) Concept: Banks' opportunity cost of holding excess reserve = interest received from loan borrowers. (2)
As there is a decrease in demand for loans, interest rate will decrease, so interest income earned by these
banks would decrease, and the cost to these banks of holding excess reserve would decrease. (2)
OR
As these banks cannot lend out their excess reserve, no interest income can be earned from this amount of
excess reserve (if there is no other alternative investment, there will be no other income too), so their cost
of holding excess reserve will be zero. (2)
(b)(ii) Some banks cannot lend out their excess reserve as the demand for bank loans decreases.
Step 1: loans that can be made by banks would decrease (1)
Step 2: money re-deposited into the banking system would decrease (1)
Correct sequence: Step 1 → Step 2 (1)
Therefore, deposit creation ability decreases. (1)
(c) Legal reserve ratio = 1/5 or 0.2 (1)
Max. deposit = $250m x 1/0.2 = $1250m (1 + 2)

questions.text:

= $(500 - 140)m x 1/20% + $50m = $1 850m
(b) Initial withdrawal of deposits
- banks lose reserves / insufficient reserves / actual reserves smaller than required reserves (1)
- banks have to call back loans / sell assets to the public (1)
- further withdrawals of deposits (1)
The process goes on and on. (1)

because when total deposits reduce to $1150 (= $1500 - $350), it only needs a reserve of $115 (= $1150 x

questions.text:
The government may reduce the money supply to cool down the overheated economy. The balance sheet of the
banking system is as follows:
Assets ($million) | Liabilities ($million)
Reserves 1 000 Deposits | 5 000
Loans | 4 000
Suppose the public in this economy always holds the same amount of cash and the banking system never holds excess
reserves. The central bank increases the minimum reserve ratio of the banks by 5%.
(a) Explain briefly the process of deposit contraction resulting from the above change in the reserve ratio.
(4 marks)
(b) Calculate and explain the change in money supply in the economy resulting from the above deposit
contraction. (5 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) An increase in the reserve ratio
=> insufficient reserves / actual reserves smaller than required reserves (1)
=> banks have to call back loans / sell assets to the public (1)
=> withdrawals of deposits (1)
The process will go on and on (until the actual reserve is equal to the required reserve). (1)
[awarded only if sequence of above steps is correct]
(b) New required reserve ratio $= 0.2 + 0.05 = 0.25$ (1)
Amount of bank deposits that $1000 million reserve can back up = $1000mn x 1/0.25 = $4000mn (1 + 1)
OR: Change of bank deposits = -$250mn x 1/0.25 = -$1000mn (1 + 1)
Change in money supply = change in cash in public (no change) + change in bank deposits (1)
therefore Change in MS $= -$1000mn (1)

questions.text:

Alternative answer:
Amount of deposits created = $100 x 1/20% = $500 (1)
therefore Total amount of deposits at maximum = $1500 (1)

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
The following table shows the balance sheet of the banking system of an economy:
Assets ($million) | Liabilities ($million)
Reserves 1 000 Deposits | 4 000
Loans | 3 000
Suppose the public in this economy always holds $500 million cash and the banking system never holds excess
reserves.
(a) Calculate the monetary base and money supply of the economy. (2 marks)
Suppose the central bank lowers the minimum reserve ratio of the banking system by 5%.
(b)(i) Explain whether the monetary base of the economy changes. (2 marks)
(b)(ii) Calculate the new money supply. Show your working. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) Monetary base = $1 000 million + $500 million = $1 500 million (1)
Money supply = $4 000 million + $500 million = $4 500 million (1)
(b)(i) No, because (1)
the policy affects neither the amount of reserves nor the cash held by the general public. (1)
(b)(ii) Before the policy change, the minimum reserve ratio = $1000 million / $4000 million = 0.25 (1)
The new minimum reserve ratio = 0.25 - 0.05 = 0.2 (1)
The banks will lend out the excess reserves.
New deposits = $1000 million x 1/0.2 = $5 000 million (1)
New money supply = $500 million + $5 000 million = $5 500 million (1)

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
The following table shows the balance sheet of the banking system of an economy.
Assets ($million) | Liabilities ($million)
Reserves | 500 Deposits | 2 000
Loans | 1 500
Suppose the public does not hold cash and there are $100 million excess reserves in the banking system.
(a) Find the required reserve ratio. Show your working. (2 marks)
(b) Find the maximum possible amount of deposits if the banks are fully loaned up. Show your working.
(2 marks)
(c) The central bank injects $200 million newly-printed banknotes into the banking system. If the banks lend
out all of their excess reserves, what will the amount of money supply be in the economy? Show your
working. (4 marks)
questions.solution:
(a) Required reserve ratio = ($500 million – $100 million) / $2 000 million (1)
= 20% (1)
(b) Maximum possible amount of deposits = $500 million × 1/0.2 (1)
= $2 500 million (1)
(c) Deposit = $700 million × 1/0.2 = $3 500 million (2)
Cash in public circulation = 0 (1)
Money supply = Deposit + Cash in public circulation = $3 500 million (1)

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
The Prime Minister of Japan, Shinzō Abe, adopted a series of policy measures in 2013 to expand the Japanese
economy. One of the policy measures was stepping up the scale of the purchase of government bonds and other
financial assets by the central bank.
(b) Describe the process of deposit creation/contraction which may result from the purchase of government
bonds by the central bank. Explain whether the process would further affect the monetary base of Japan.
(5 marks)
questions.solution:
(b) Credit creation process:
When the central bank purchases bonds from commercial banks, more cash is injected to the commercial
banks as reserves and there would be excess reserves in the banking system. (1)
The banks would lend out the excess reserves. (1)
And the bank loans will be re-deposited into the banking system. (1)
The process will go on and on (until the actual reserves are equal to required reserves).
No. The monetary base will remain unchanged as the sum of cash in public circulation and reserves in the
banking system will not be affected by the credit creation process. (2)

questions.text:
Study the following balance sheet of the banking system in Country A.
Assets ($million) | Liabilities ($million)
Reserves 1 000 Deposits | 5 000

(b) Calculate the new monetary base in Country A. Show your workings. (2 marks)
(c) Calculate the new money supply in Country A. Show your workings. (3 marks)
questions.solution:
(a)(i) Legal Reserve ratio = $1000 million / $5000 million = 0.2 (1)
(a)(ii) Money supply = $150 million + $5000 million = $5150 million (2)
(b) New monetary base = $150 million + $1050 million = $1200 million (2)
(c) New money supply = $150 million + $1050 million / 0.2 = $5400 million (3)

questions.subject: Macro
questions.text:
The following is the balance sheet of a banking system
Assets ($million) | Liabilities ($million)
Reserves 1 000 Deposits | 4 000
Loans | 3 000
Suppose the public always holds $500 million of cash and the banking system does not hold excess reserves.
(a) Calculate the monetary base and money supply. (2 marks)
The central bank increases the required reserve ratio to 50%.
(b) Calculate the change in monetary base and the change in money supply. Show your working. (4 marks)
(c)(i) Why is money supply often a few times more than monetary base? (3 marks)
(c)(ii) Under what situation will money supply be equal to monetary base? (1 mark)
questions.solution:
(a) Monetary base = $500 million + $1000 million = $1500 million (1)
Money supply = $500 million + $4000 million = $4500 million (1)
(b) Change in monetary base = $1500 million – $1500 million = 0 (2)
Change in money supply
= New money supply – Original money supply
= ($500 million + $1000 million × 2) – $4500 million = –$2000 million (2)
or
Change in money supply
= Change in cash held by non-bank public + Change in deposits
= 0 + ($1000 million × 2 – $4000 million) = –$2000 million (2)
(c)(i) Under a fractional reserve banking system, banks are required to keep only a fraction of their deposits as
reserves. They can create credit by lending out the remaining fraction in the form of loans to businesses
and private individuals, which would eventually find their way back into the banking system in the form
of deposits, resulting in a multiple increase in deposits/a banking multiplier larger than unity. (3)
(c)(ii) If the legal reserve ratio is 100% (RRR=1) or if all of the banks decide not to lend out their excess reserves
even when RRR<1 (e.g. during financial crisis, when default rates are high), the money supply will be
equal to the monetary base. (1)
